gainsay

GAYN-say · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To gainsay is to deny or contradict a fact or statement.

No one at the town meeting was willing to gainsay the fire chief's blunt assessment of the building's safety.

Example

When the new hire noticed the official sales report listed the wrong total, she calmly gainsaid the number in front of the whole team.

Gainsaying isn't just disagreeing quietly -- it means openly stating that a claim or fact is wrong.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

contradict: To contradict is to state the opposite of what someone else has said, and even two reports or witnesses can contradict each other without anyone intending it. To gainsay is always a deliberate act: a person openly denying that a claim or fact is true. Contradiction can be accidental; gainsaying never is.

dispute: To dispute a statement is to question or challenge its truth, opening an argument that both sides can still press. To gainsay is blunter: flatly denying the statement outright, insisting it is simply wrong. Disputing invites a debate; gainsaying issues a denial.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

affirm: to state firmly that something is true

corroborate: to support a claim with evidence

Where it sits · how forcefully the claim is challenged — question → gainsay → refute

question vs. gainsay: To question something is only to raise doubt about it, a milder response than flatly gainsaying it.

refute vs. gainsay: To refute something is to prove it false with solid evidence or logic, a much stronger response than simply gainsaying it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — gain-

prefix — gain-: against, contrary (an old word, unrelated to the everyday verb 'gain') (Old English gegn)

root — say

root — say: to declare, to state (Old English secgan)

Put it together

Put it together: Gainsay combines the old prefix gain- ('against,' completely unrelated to the everyday verb 'gain,' as in to gain money) with say -- literally 'to say against,' which is exactly what gainsay means: to deny or contradict.

Use the root in a new word: unsaid

Use the root in a new word: unsaid: Everyone agreed the new mascot costume looked a little ungainly under the gym lights.

Root Check

Word Choice

Careful: the 'gain' in gainsay has nothing to do with the everyday verb gain (to acquire) -- it's an old word meaning 'against.' Gainsay itself is fairly formal and a bit old-fashioned, often used in the phrase 'no one can gainsay that...'
